title: Drawing & Composition: Stretch
welcome_lead: Push beyond the basics — atmospheric perspective, dynamic balance and intentional composition.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE drawing skills: atmospheric perspective, asymmetric balance, foreshortening.
final_note: These advanced tools let you design images that feel inevitable.

concepts.def: Distant objects look paler, bluer, less sharp.
Compressing a form to show it angled towards viewer.
Visual weight balanced without mirroring sides.
The flat surface the artist works on.
The angle from which the subject is observed.
Cutting the frame to focus on part of the subject.

walkthroughs.body_html: Air contains moisture and dust, so distant things lose contrast, shift bluer and soften. Use this in landscapes: keep your foreground crisp and dark, your background pale and hazy. It works alongside linear perspective for convincing depth.
When a limb points towards you, it appears compressed. Draw what you see, not what you know — measure the visible length, exaggerate the closest forms slightly and overlap shapes to imply depth.

A composition does not need to be symmetrical to feel balanced. A large pale shape on one side can be balanced by a small dark accent on the other — visual weight matters more than size. Cropping tightens that balance.
